gloss: Setsubun; day before the beginning of spring

definitions.gloss: Setsubun; the day before the start of spring
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese event held on February 3rd (occasionally February 2nd), marking the transition from winter to spring in the old calendar. People throw roasted soybeans to drive away evil spirits, shouting '{鬼|おに}は{外|そと}、{福|ふく}は{内|うち}' (Demons out, fortune in).

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{節分|せつぶん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{恵方巻|えほうまき}→恵方巻：22491_ehoumaki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: This year on Setsubun, the whole family ate ehomaki rolls.
On the night of Setsubun, we threw beans, calling out "Demons out, good luck in!"

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Originally the day before any of the four seasonal divisions; now it means the day before ⟦{立春|りっしゅん}→立春：22417_risshun⟧ (the start of spring), usually February 3.
- ⟦{豆|まめ}まき→豆まき：14275_mamemaki⟧: throwing roasted soybeans to drive out ⟦{鬼|おに}→鬼：02184_oni⟧, calling 「⟦{鬼|おに}→鬼：02184_oni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{外|そと}→外：00671_soto⟧、{福|ふく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{内|うち}→内：01328_uchi⟧」
- eating as many beans as one's age (in some homes, one more) for good health
- eating a whole ⟦{恵方巻|えほうまき}→恵方巻：22491_ehoumaki⟧ sushi roll in silence, facing the year's lucky direction
Temples and shrines hold public bean-throwing events, often with celebrities and sumo wrestlers.
